documents.title: Guidelines for AI Use at The City College of New York
documents.summary: The College guidelines are advisory ('not policy') and say that each syllabus must state the instructor's own AI rules, which differ by class. They also set declaration, data-privacy and assessment advice. The College does not set a default for or against AI use.
documents.stance_why: The guidelines say they are "not policy" and that "it is essential that your syllabus include your own guidelines for the acceptable use of AI tools", with the line "likely to be different in different classes". No default ban or permission is set at college level, so the decision is delegated to instructors.

documents.title: CUNY Academic Integrity Policy (2024)
documents.summary: CUNY's system-wide Academic Integrity Policy (2024) adds AI to its definitions of cheating and plagiarism: unauthorized AI use, AI-generated content without citation, and AI in exams are violations. Instructors may authorize AI use in the syllabus. Procedures and sanctions are the general ones.
documents.stance_why: The policy defines "using artificial intelligence tools to generate content for assignments or exams ... without written authorization from the instructor" as cheating, so AI is banned unless authorized; this is restrict. It does not itself offer tiers or hand out templates.

units.why: The cheating definition includes "unauthorized use ... of ... artificial intelligence (AI) systems" during an academic exercise. It classifies unauthorized AI use as cheating (P36) and applies to students.
